editorial.meta_description: The ACCA Financial Management exam is scheduled for retirement on 2027-06-30 and will be replaced by the E4 exam for all certification candidates.
editorial.overview: The Financial Management (FM/F9) exam, certified by the ACCA, covers the financial management function, financial analysis, financing decisions, investments, and business valuations. It evaluates technical proficiency in managing corporate finance, including working capital, risk management, and capital structure. As this exam is scheduled for retirement on 2027-06-30, students must prepare for the successor exam, E4, to ensure their professional certification path remains current and aligned with ACCA requirements. This assessment ensures that candidates possess the skills to navigate financial environments while maintaining the standards expected by the ACCA organization for all its certified finance professionals.
editorial.who_should_take: This exam is intended for accounting students and finance professionals seeking to demonstrate competency in corporate financial management. Candidates should possess practical experience in financial analysis and investment appraisal to succeed in this 180-minute assessment.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Review the official technical articles and topic explainers provided by the ACCA. Practice both Objective Test Questions and Constructed Response tasks to build speed. Ensure you understand the application of the Capital Asset Pricing Model and working capital management. Given the 202 dollar price, focus on mastering the syllabus early. Since the exam retires on 2027-06-30, prioritize the E4 curriculum for long-term planning. Consistent practice and review of all core financial concepts are needed for achieving success on this professional certification exam.

domain_guidance.summary: This domain covers the role and purpose of the financial management function within an organization, focusing on how financial managers contribute to business objectives, stakeholder value, and the economic environment in which the firm operates for long-term success.

This domain involves the detailed analysis of financial data to assess business performance, liquidity, and solvency, providing insights into the overall financial health and operational efficiency of an organization for stakeholders and internal management decision-making processes.

This domain focuses on identifying and evaluating alternative sources of business finance, including debt and equity, while determining the optimal capital structure to support long-term growth and minimize the cost of capital for the firm in various scenarios.

This domain covers investment appraisal techniques, including net present value and internal rate of return, to assist in long-term project decision-making while accounting for the impacts of inflation and taxation on future cash flows for the organization.

This domain addresses the principles of business and asset valuations, utilizing various models to determine the value of equity and debt in different scenarios, ensuring accurate financial reporting and strategic decision-making capabilities for the business entity.

editorial.exam_day_guidance: The exam is a 180-minute linear assessment. You will encounter Objective Test Questions and Constructed Response items. Ensure you reach the 50 passing score by managing your time across all sections effectively to demonstrate your full competency.

faq.question_title: How many questions are on the exam?
faq.answer_text: The exam utilizes a linear format consisting of Objective Test Questions and Constructed Response tasks. Candidates must manage their time across these formats during the 180-minute duration to reach the 50 passing score, ensuring all required areas of the syllabus are addressed.

To successfully pass the Financial Management (FM/F9) exam, candidates must achieve a minimum score of 50. This threshold is set to ensure that all certified professionals demonstrate a sufficient level of technical knowledge and practical application skills.

The Financial Management (FM/F9) exam is a 180-minute assessment. Candidates are expected to manage their time effectively throughout this period to complete all Objective Test Questions and Constructed Response tasks required to achieve the passing score.

faq.question_title: What is the replacement for this exam?
faq.answer_text: The verified successor to the Financial Management (FM/F9) exam is E4. The ACCA has scheduled the retirement of FM/F9 for 2027-06-30, and candidates should plan their certification path to align with this transition to the new E4 curriculum.
